The pair is intentional:\n\n- `home` is the `HomeIsolation` instance — primitives that need `home.env()` (e.g. `Expect.settings_json` traversing `~/.claude/settings.json`) or `home.state_path(...)` (helpers that join a suffix safely) call it directly.\n- `home_path` is a `Path` — primitives that only need the directory avoid the `home.home_path` property indirection *and* the `RuntimeError` it raises when setup has not run (by the time the factory builds the context, setup has already completed and dereferencing the property always succeeds).\n\nThe factory enforces `home.home_path == home_path` as an invariant so the two never drift.\n\n### Factory keyword-only arguments\n\n`from_runner_state` is defined with `*` before the first parameter so every argument must be passed by keyword. Rationale: future field additions (e.g. when DM-010 grows a 16th field for OQ-8 wall-clock plumbing) would silently re-bind positional callers if we did not enforce this. The cost is a slightly longer call site in `EvalRunner` (T03.04); the benefit is that any test or runner that constructs a context fails loudly the moment the schema changes. Covered by `test_from_runner_state_keyword_only_arguments`.\n\n### Factory raises through `home.home_path` rather than building a half-valid context\n\n`HomeIsolation.home_path` raises `RuntimeError(\"HomeIsolation.setup() must be called before accessing home_path\")` when setup has not run. Two options:\n\n1. **Catch the `RuntimeError` and fabricate a placeholder** (e.g. `Path(\"/\")`). Rejected — half-valid contexts are worse than no context. An ExpectCallable that read the placeholder would silently produce garbage assertions.\n2. **Let the `RuntimeError` propagate** (chosen). The factory call site (`EvalRunner.run`) is the right place to fail loudly — by the time the runner builds the context the setup step is supposed to have completed, so a propagation here is a runner-internal bug, not a user-facing error. Covered by `test_from_runner_state_raises_when_home_not_setup`.\n\n### Why no `to_dict()` for `EvalContext`\n\nDM-001 (`EvalOutcome`) and DM-003 (`EvalResult`) have `to_dict()` because they flow into JSON artifacts (`summary.json`). DM-010 (`EvalContext`) is consumed in-process by ExpectCallables; none of the downstream Reporter paths serialise it. Adding `to_dict()` for symmetry would be dead code today and would force us to define serialisation for `EvalSpec` and `HomeIsolation`, both of which carry richer state than what the Reporter needs. The `_EVAL_CONTEXT_FIELDS` constant is still in place so a future `to_dict()` can iterate in DM-010 order if the need arises.\n\n### Module-level vs. delayed `HomeIsolation` import\n\n`HomeIsolation` is imported from `.isolation`, which itself imports from `.loader` (for `validate_eval_id`) and `.config` (for `EvalConfig`). To avoid the import cycle that would land if `models.py` imported `isolation.py` eagerly, the `HomeIsolation` import is guarded by `TYPE_CHECKING` and the dataclass field uses a forward-string annotation (`\"HomeIsolation\"`). Runtime construction works because the factory accepts the instance as a keyword argument and never has to introspect the class.\n\n## Future work touchpoints\n\n- **T03.04 / T03.05 (EvalRunner)** — primary construction site for `EvalContext`. The runner will call `EvalContext.from_runner_state(...)` after the `observe` lifecycle step has captured stdout/stderr/exit_code, then pass the context to each `Expect.*` callable in the `assert` step.\n- **T04.01..T04.07 (Expect primitives)** — every primitive is a function from `EvalContext` to `ExpectResult`. The 15-field contract is the surface they read; primitives that need helpers (`home.state_path`, `home.env`) call them off the `home` field.\n- **OQ-8 (DOC-OQ8 / T06.03)** — when wall-clock offset semantics resolve, the runner may need to thread an additional field through the context; `_EVAL_CONTEXT_FIELDS` provides the canonical insertion point.\n","numLines":50,"startLine":1,"totalLines":50}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BzLkBLMogLDm5q5qCcy91S","type":"tool_result","content":"# D-0048 — FR-LC1 EvalRunner lifecycle spec\n\n**Task:** T03.04 (Phase 3, Roadmap FR-LC1 / R-048)\n**Module:** `src/superclaude/cli/eval/runner.py`\n**Status:** Implemented 2026-05-20\n\n## Scope\n\nT03.04 lands the FR-LC1 *lifecycle skeleton*: a single entrypoint\n`run_eval(spec, ...) -> EvalOutcome` that executes the seven-step per-eval\nsequence and enforces the status-mapping rules. The runner *class* that\nCOMP-004 (T03.05) layers on top — per-eval JSONL logging, per-eval\ntimeout, parallel orchestration handoff — is explicitly out of scope here\n(see §\"Out of scope for T03.04\" below).\n\nThe skeleton is fully testable without a real PTY: the spawn / inject /\nobserve trio is injected as a `LifecycleExecutor` protocol so unit tests\nsubstitute stubs that return canned exit codes and transcripts. T03.05\nplugs in the concrete `PtyDriver` + `ClaudeProcessAdapter` executor.\n\n## 7-step lifecycle (FR-LC1)\n\nThe sequence below is executed verbatim by `run_eval`. Each step name\nmatches the design-spec diagram (`design-spec.md §6`) and the roadmap row\n(R-048) so artefact lookups stay grepable.\n\n| # | Step | Implementation site | Allowed exception → status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **build isolation** | `HomeIsolation.setup(config=...)` (T02.11 / D-0032). Atomic-setup wrapper (T02.13) is honoured — partial HOMEs stay on disk for forensics. | `HomeContainmentViolation` / `RuntimeError` / `OSError` → **ERRORED** (`teardown(keep=True)`). |\n| 2 | **deploy hooks** | `deploy_hooks_to(home_path)` (T02.14 / D-0034). Caller-injectable so tests stub the deploy without a real `hooks.json`. | `HookDeployFailed` / `OSError` → **ERRORED** (`teardown(keep=True)`). |\n| 3 | **spawn** | `executor.spawn(ctx)` — production wires `ClaudeProcessAdapter.spawn()` + `PtyDriver.spawn()` (T02.16 / T02.19). | Any `BaseException` other than `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` → **ERRORED** (`teardown(keep=True)`). `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` propagates so NFR-REL1 (T03.07) can mark **INTERRUPTED**. |\n| 4 | **inject** | `executor.inject(ctx, prompts)` — production wires `PtyDriver.inject_prompt` and the manifest's `inputs[*]`. | Same propagation rule as step 3. |\n| 5 | **observe** | `executor.observe(ctx) -> ObservedRun` — production drains `PtyDriver.read_stdout` until exit and captures `(stdout, stderr, exit_code, duration_sec, transcript_path)`. Per-eval JSONL log lives in T03.05; per-eval timeout lives in T03.07. | `TimeoutError` reserved for T03.07 → **TIMEOUT** (skeleton routes through `ERRORED` mapping today; T03.07 swaps the branch). Other exceptions → **ERRORED**. |\n| 6 | **assert** | Each `ExpectCallable(ctx)` (FR-EXP1 / T04.01..T04.07 land later) is invoked. The runner builds an `EvalContext` via `EvalContext.from_runner_state(...)` (T03.03) once observe returns and passes it to every callable. | Any callable that raises → **ERRORED** with `error_class = \"<fqcn>\"`. Any callable that returns an `ExpectResult` with `passed=False` → **FAIL**. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01GXBSobHCeH8BF69A7Z1sGF","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01KV4QD9gU9xsxE5PNphqX9Z","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/config/workspace/IronClaude/.dev/releases/current/cliEval/artifacts/D-0048/notes.md","content":"# D-0048 — FR-LC1 EvalRunner lifecycle implementation notes\n\n## Design decisions\n\n### `LifecycleExecutor` Protocol vs. concrete class\n\nThe runner skeleton must be testable without spinning up a real\n`PtyDriver` + `ClaudeProcessAdapter`. Three shapes were considered:\n\n1. **Concrete `EvalRunner` class with PTY hard-wired** — rejected:\n   forces every lifecycle unit test to build a fake PTY, and bakes\n   COMP-004 (T03.05) details into a T03.04 deliverable.\n2. **Function with a single `spawn_observe(...)` callable** —\n   rejected: collapses three distinct lifecycle phases (spawn / inject\n   / observe per design-spec §6) into one callable, so the runner can\n   no longer distinguish \"spawn failed\" from \"observe failed\" in the\n   `error_class` field, and tests cannot assert that step 3 ran but\n   step 4 did not.\n3. **Protocol with three methods** (chosen) — `LifecycleExecutor`\n   surfaces `spawn(ctx) -> None`, `inject(ctx) -> None`, and\n   `observe(ctx) -> ObservedRun`. Production wiring (T03.05) plugs in\n   a `PtyClaudeExecutor` that delegates to `ClaudeProcessAdapter` +\n   `PtyDriver`; tests substitute a `RecordingExecutor`.\n\nThe Protocol is *structural*: no `register()` call needed. Pythonic\nduck typing means `RecordingExecutor` does not need to inherit from\n`LifecycleExecutor`; a single `_PROTOCOL_CHECK: LifecycleExecutor =\nRecordingExecutor()` in the test file pins the structural conformance\nso a future field addition fails the test at import time.\n\n### `ExecutorContext` vs. raw arguments\n\nThe executor needs a stable handle on the per-eval HOME, the run\npaths, and the env overlay. Two options:\n\n1. **Pass each path as a positional argument to `spawn`** — rejected:\n   adding a new path (e.g. T03.05's per-eval JSONL log) is a breaking\n   change for every executor implementation, including test stubs.\n2. **Frozen `ExecutorContext` dataclass** (chosen) — bundles\n   `eval_spec`, `home`, `home_path`, `run_dir`, `artifacts_dir`,\n   `stdout_path`, `stderr_path`, `transcript_path`, and `env`. Future\n   field additions are non-breaking for executors that ignore them;\n   T03.05 can grow the context with `jsonl_log_path` without\n   touching `RecordingExecutor`.\n\n`ExecutorContext` is intentionally distinct from `EvalContext`\n(DM-010 / T03.03): the executor sees the pre-observe view (no\nexit_code yet), the ExpectCallables see the post-observe view (15\nfields, exit_code populated). Mixing them would force the executor to\neither dereference fields that do not yet exist or accept a\nhalf-populated record.\n\n### `ObservedRun` carries `artifacts` and `jsonl_paths`\n\n`ObservedRun` is the *executor return type* and is folded into both\n`EvalOutcome.artifacts` and `EvalContext.{jsonl_paths,artifacts}`.\nThe choice to model these as `Mapping` fields with `MappingProxyType`-\ncompatible defaults mirrors the same immutability discipline the\nDM-010 `EvalContext` uses (T03.03 / D-0047): an executor that returns\nan `ObservedRun` containing a plain `dict` cannot be mutated by the\nrunner after-the-fact (the dataclass is frozen) but the runner *can*\nre-wrap the mapping in `MappingProxyType` before threading it into\n`EvalContext.from_runner_state(...)` — and does.\n\n### Per-step `try`/`except` rather than a single outer `try`\n\nThe status mapping requires the runner to know *which* step raised so\n`error_class` reflects the exception's classname and so the\nstatus-mapping helper can distinguish \"observe never ran\" (pin\n`duration_sec` to 0.0) from \"observe ran but an Expect raised\" (keep\nthe observed duration). Three options:\n\n1. **Outer `try`/`except` only** — rejected: forces the classification\n   helper to inspect the traceback to figure out which step raised.\n2. **One `try`/`except` per step with a shared `_finalize` exit**\n   (chosen) — each step's `except` calls `state.record_harness_failure(\n   step=..., exc=...)` then returns through `_finalize(...)`. The\n   classification helper reads `state.harness_failure_step` to decide\n   whether to pin `duration_sec` to 0.0.\n3. **`with`-style context manager per step** — rejected: the\n   `__exit__` would either need to re-raise (defeating the capture)\n   or swallow (defeating SIGINT propagation). The plain `try`/`except`\n   stays simpler.\n\n### `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` propagation\n\nNFR-REL1 (T03.07) requires cooperative cancellation: the orchestrator\ninstalls a signal handler that converts `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` into a\n`KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` raised inside the runner. The\nrunner MUST NOT classify these as `ERRORED` — they are a graceful\nshutdown signal, not a harness bug. Three options:\n\n1. **Re-raise from every `except`** (chosen) — each per-step\n   `except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit): raise` re-raises before\n   the broad `except BaseException` runs. The outer `try`/`except`\n   then catches `(KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit)` to run\n   `_safe_teardown(home, keep=True)` before re-raising again. The\n   orchestrator's signal handler converts the propagated exception\n   into an `INTERRUPTED` outcome at the suite layer.\n2. **Catch and convert to `EvalOutcome(status=\"INTERRUPTED\")`** —\n   rejected: the runner cannot tell whether the orchestrator is also\n   tearing down. Returning an outcome when the process is mid-\n   shutdown would leak the partial summary to the Reporter and cause\n   the harness to \"succeed\" through a Ctrl-C.\n3. **Catch only `KeyboardInterrupt`, let `SystemExit` propagate\n   untouched** — rejected: NFR-REL1 must cover both signals\n   uniformly. Diverging behaviour for the two would surprise\n   operators.\n\n### Teardown is best-effort (does NOT flip status)\n\nThe design-spec invariant is \"teardown is best-effort\": a failing\nteardown must not flip `PASS` to `FAIL`. Three options:\n\n1. **Re-raise the teardown exception** — rejected: a permissions\n   error in `shutil.rmtree` would convert every clean PASS into an\n   error, which contradicts the spec.\n2. **Capture the exception silently** — rejected: losing the\n   traceback makes debugging cleanup bugs impossible.\n3. **Swallow with optional `on_teardown_error` callback** (chosen) —\n   the callback is `Optional[Callable[[BaseException], None]]`; the\n   COMP-004 runner class (T03.05) plugs in a callback that writes the\n   exception to its per-eval JSONL log.
